solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bloke bound to succeed getting hold of iron cow

indicators.note: a word that gets hold of something grips it inside itself, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: an heir is the man who will succeed to a title or estate
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A man destined to inherit the farm is seen gripping a cow made of iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloke bound to succeed' reads as a man sure to do well, but it means someone due to succeed to an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A heifer is a young female bovine that has not yet calved, a kind of cow.

clue.text: Kind about eccentricity of a Scottish thinker

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the next piece

blocks.note: humankind; the human kind
e is the mathematical symbol for the eccentricity of a conic section

explanation.surface: A kindly word about the eccentric habits of a Scottish philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: E sits inside HUMAN. 'Eccentricity' suggests oddness, but it is the geometric quantity written e.
explanation.definitionFit: Humean means relating to David Hume, the eighteenth-century Scottish philosopher.

clue.text: Singer losing her head for fine gentleman

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter is cut off

blocks.note: Bette Midler is an American singer and actress

explanation.surface: A female singer is beheaded in place of an elegant gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Her' tells you the singer is a woman: Bette Midler.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler is a man of leisure, which is what a fine gentleman with no need to work was.

clue.text: Stood in awe of fine European pressing a type of wine

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
E is the abbreviation for European
taken as written
red is a type of wine

explanation.surface: A wine lover revered a fine European treading grapes for red.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'pressing' puts FE on top of A and RED.
explanation.definitionFit: To fear can mean to revere or hold in awe, as in fearing God.

clue.text: Logically therefore I will enter run

indicators.note: a piece that will enter goes inside the other

blocks.note: the ego is the self, the I
R is the abbreviation for run in cricket

explanation.surface: A logician concludes that he must enter the race.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside EGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore, used to introduce a logical conclusion.

clue.text: Constant delay developing purified sugar, say

definitions.note: a past-participle phrase: clayed means treated with clay, as sugar was

indicators.note: something developing is changing form, so the following letters are reworked

blocks.note: c is the symbol for a constant, e.g. the speed of light
the letters of delay, rearranged

explanation.surface: A constant hold-up in refining sugar at a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: Raw sugar was once refined by covering it with wet clay, which washed out the molasses; such sugar was called clayed.
explanation.definitionFit: To clay sugar is to refine it with a clay wash, so clayed describes sugar purified that way.

clue.text: Lace silken cords joined between strands?

indicators.note: to lace is to weave threads in and out, so the letters are interwoven anew

blocks.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: Silk cords are threaded through lace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lace' looks like the fabric in the picture, but it is the instruction to work the next words' letters together.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry, cross-linked polymer chains are bonded to each other by links running between the strands.

clue.text: Spinach filling most of old platter with pasta dish

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its last letter
a filling goes inside, so the first word is placed within the other

blocks.note: sag is spinach in Indian cookery, as in sag aloo
lanx is a Roman platter or dish
the setter's draft read 'with a', and that a supplied this letter; it was lost when the clue was amended

explanation.surface: Spinach fills an old serving dish beside a plate of pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as printed is a letter short: the setter's original read 'with a pasta dish', and the 'a' that gives the final letter was lost in an editing amendment.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagna is a baked dish of layered flat pasta sheets with sauce.

clue.text: Bumpkins picking up reed, approved as stuffing

indicators.note: in a down entry, picking up means lifting, so the word reads from bottom to top
stuffing goes inside, so the next piece is put within the other

blocks.note: a sley is a weaver's reed
OK means approved

explanation.surface: Country folk gather reeds and pass them fit for stuffing a mattress.
explanation.walkthrough: A sley is the comb-like reed of a weaving loom, not a riverside plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Yokels are unsophisticated country people, the same as bumpkins.

clue.text: With rent adjusted fail over special mezzanines

indicators.note: something adjusted has been rearranged, so these letters change order
turned over means flipped, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: the letters of rent, rearranged
to fail is to lose
S is the abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: Mezzanine flats fail once the rent is raised.
explanation.definitionFit: An entresol is a low storey between two main floors, which is a mezzanine.

clue.text: Flowers I plucked forming canopies over altars and similar

indicators.note: something plucked is pulled out, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: daisies are flowers
taken as written

explanation.surface: Flowers are picked to decorate canopies over altars.
explanation.walkthrough: One I comes out of DAISIES.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais can be a canopy over a throne or altar, as well as a raised platform.

clue.text: Student is out — good, excellent

blocks.note: someone who is out cold under anaesthetic is under
G is the abbreviation for good
rad is slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A report on a student who has graduated or left, judged good and excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' looks like 'away from college', but it means unconscious, as a patient under anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: An undergrad is a university student who has not yet taken a first degree.

clue.text: Mock up game woefully missing one with a wordy way

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top
missing one means the letter I is left out

blocks.note: to rag is to tease or mock
RU is rugby union
lousily means badly or woefully

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a game played badly, missing one, and rambles on about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Garrulously means talkatively, in a long-winded manner.

clue.text: Drink most of whisky in front of kitchen range

indicators.note: most of a word means all of it except the final letter

blocks.note: malt is a malt whisky
an Aga is a brand of heavy cast-iron kitchen range cooker common in British homes

explanation.surface: Someone drinks most of the whisky by the warm kitchen stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink' looks like a verb opening the sentence, but it is the noun being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaga is a sweet fortified wine from the Spanish province of that name, so it is a drink.

clue.text: From the east, it is about Kali's aspect primarily

definitions.text: From the east, it is about Kali's aspect primarily

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letters of the words it follows
about means around, so the first piece wraps the second
in an across entry, coming from the east means read from right to left

blocks.note: it is contracts to it's
the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: An Eastern religious statement about one aspect of the goddess Kali.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: Sakti is the divine female energy, of which Kali is a fierce aspect, and the concept comes from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hinduism Sakti (Shakti) is the female creative power of a god, worshipped in forms such as Kali.

clue.text: Bill holding right juicy fruit up is to interject abruptly?

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside
in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a bird's bill is its beak
R is the abbreviation for right
noni is a juicy tropical fruit

explanation.surface: A bird with fruit in its beak is a cue to butt in.
explanation.walkthrough: Noni is the fruit of a Pacific tree, sold as a health juice.
explanation.definitionFit: To break in on a conversation is to interrupt it suddenly.

clue.text: Small dosh (all but hundred bucks) for birds of prey

indicators.note: all but a hundred means remove the Roman numeral for a hundred

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
ackers is British slang for money, like dosh

explanation.surface: Someone spends a little cash, nearly a hundred dollars, on hawks.
explanation.walkthrough: C, the Roman hundred, comes out of ACKERS. Dosh and ackers are both British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Sakers are large falcons, so they are birds of prey.

clue.text: Debt is arranged till no longer left to spiral

indicators.note: the letter on the left of a word is its first, so only that is kept

blocks.note: arr. is the abbreviation for arranged, as on sheet music
ear is an obsolete verb meaning to plough or till
the leftmost letter of the word

explanation.surface: A debt is restructured so that it no longer spirals out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' marks the word as archaic: to ear the land was to plough it.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrears are money owed that is overdue, so they amount to a debt.

clue.text: Joy in grand old tranquillity

blocks.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
lee is an obsolete word for shelter or calm

explanation.surface: Delight found in the peace of a grand old house.
explanation.definitionFit: Glee is a feeling of great delight, a synonym of joy.

clue.text: The condition of wanting fun and sense led afresh

indicators.note: doing something afresh means making it over again, so the letters are laid out anew

blocks.note: the letters of the three words, with and as a joiner

explanation.surface: A life of wanting, where fun and good sense lead the way once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' only joins the two fodder pieces fun and sense led.
explanation.definitionFit: Needfulness is the state of being in need, so it is a condition of wanting or lacking something.

clue.text: Displeasure died in dull bar offering support

indicators.note: in places the previous pieces inside the next one

blocks.note: to fog is to dull or cloud
ire is anger or displeasure
d. is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: Annoyance dies down in a gloomy pub that offers a friendly ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub in the surface, but here it is a metal bar in a fireplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A firedog is a metal stand, also called an andiron, that supports logs in a fireplace.

clue.text: Figure of speech is back by not a small distance?

indicators.note: back tells you to read the word in the opposite direction

blocks.note: taken as written
a mile is quite a long way

explanation.surface: A figure of speech returns, describing a long way back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a small distance' is a deliberate understatement, itself a figure of speech, for a fair way.
explanation.definitionFit: A simile is a figure of speech comparing one thing to another with 'like' or 'as'.

clue.text: Condition of Italian if out of sorts

definitions.note: loose: affiliation is the state of being attached to a body

indicators.note: being out of sorts means being upset or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Wondering about an Italian's health if he is feeling unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'of' after 'Condition' is part of the fodder, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Affiliation is the state of being connected to an organisation, a status or condition of membership.

clue.text: Performer preposterously with whopper about King

indicators.note: preposterous literally means before-behind, last put first, so the word is turned round
about means around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: of can mean with, as in 'a man of means'
a whopper is a big lie
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: An entertainer is absurdly accompanied by a giant tale about a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Preposterously is read in its Latin root sense, prae + posterus, before-after: the first letter is put last.
explanation.definitionFit: A folkie is an informal word for a folk musician, who is a performer.

clue.text: Boozers not displaying Nationalist Scotsman's ribbons

indicators.note: not displaying something means it is left out

blocks.note: boozers are pubs, which are taverns
N is the abbreviation for Nationalist

explanation.surface: Pubs refuse to show the Scottish Nationalists' banners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boozers' looks like drinkers, but in British slang a boozer is a pub. TAVERS is a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, tavers (taivers) are tatters or shreds, so they are ribbons in the sense of strips.

clue.text: Not sufficient funds? Clear defunct academic set-up in short

blocks.note: NSF is the banking abbreviation for not sufficient funds
net means clear, as in clear profit

explanation.surface: A bounced cheque clears an old university network out.
explanation.definitionFit: NSFNET was the US National Science Foundation's academic computer network, a forerunner of the internet now shut down.

clue.text: Flabbergasted oik associated with new smiley, say

indicators.note: someone flabbergasted is thrown into confusion, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: oik is British slang for a boorish person
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: An astonished lout is linked with a fresh smiley face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Associated with' sits between the anagrammed word and the single extra letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikon is a variant spelling of icon, and a smiley is an example of a small screen icon.

clue.text: Scoutherings feasible leading to cries amongst harpooneers

blocks.note: on means possible, as in 'that's not on'
fall is the whalers' cry when a whale is sighted or struck

explanation.surface: Shouts among whale-hunters about Scottish weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Scouthering and onfall are both Scots words for a light fall of rain or snow.
explanation.definitionFit: An onfall is a Scots term for a shower of rain or snow, the same thing as a scouthering.

clue.text: On which to sit when finding discharges

blocks.note: a lav is a lavatory, something you sit on
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A seat on which to sit when you find yourself relieved.
explanation.walkthrough: The toilet humour of the surface is deliberate: LAV is short for lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavas are the molten rock discharged by volcanoes.

clue.text: I am back in place of setting

indicators.note: going back means reading from right to left

blocks.note: I am contracts to I'm
lieu means place, as in 'in lieu of'

explanation.surface: Someone returns to the place where the story is set.
explanation.walkthrough: IM is read backwards and followed by LIEU.
explanation.definitionFit: A milieu is a person's surroundings, the setting in which they live or act.

clue.text: Grass is top class in hearing

indicators.note: what something sounds like in a listener's hearing, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: alpha means first-rate, as in alpha male

explanation.surface: The lawn is top quality, to listen to people.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfa is esparto, a tough grass grown in North Africa and Spain for paper-making.

clue.text: Half must depart cheated for having tattoos?

indicators.note: half departing means the front half of the word is taken away

blocks.note: to hoodwink is to deceive

explanation.surface: Half the gang leave after being cheated, and they look heavily tattooed.
explanation.walkthrough: HOODWINKED has ten letters; removing the first five leaves INKED.
explanation.definitionFit: Inked is slang for tattooed, since tattoos are made with ink; the question mark flags the slang.

clue.text: Side moving back to front in defence of Mississippi before noon

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is moved round to its start

blocks.note: levees are the embankments that hold back the Mississippi
N is the abbreviation for noon, and 'before' places it after the moved letters

explanation.surface: A team moves its defence back to protect the Mississippi before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: The final E of LEVEE moves to the front, giving ELEVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket or football side has eleven players, so a team is called an eleven.

clue.text: Cutting celebrity once take's canned for box, for protection

indicators.note: something canned is sealed inside a tin, so one piece is put inside the other

blocks.note: a cutting wind is a cold one
fame means celebrity
R stands for Latin recipe, 'take', heading old prescriptions

explanation.surface: A one-time celebrity's take is axed as a protective measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canned' suggests sacked, but it means enclosed, as in a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold frame is a glass-topped box that protects young plants from frost.

clue.text: Generally losing everything stimulated vigorous activity

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken out of the word
something stimulated is stirred up, so the letters are shaken into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
all means everything

explanation.surface: Losing everything usually sparked a burst of frantic activity.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL comes out of GENERALLY, leaving GENERY to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Energy is vigour and capacity for action, so it describes vigorous activity.

clue.text: Fred, for example, is born with property

blocks.note: b. is the abbreviation for born
an asset is a piece of property

explanation.surface: A man called Fred is born into wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: Fred is not a person: Fred Basset is a basset hound in a long-running British newspaper comic strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Basset is the cartoon example of a basset, a short-legged hound.
